note: All three v3 games ended the same way. The extractor ignored info.lagMs (about 45 ms), so a tap chosen on a 'pop' frame landed 2-3 frames (about 8 deg) later. That put it 8-12 deg past the dot (the end screens show the bar about 11 deg past). askWhen also consulted the engine from the first 'edge' frame, which pushed the next decision about 45 ms away just when one-frame precision was needed. The extractor now places every bar feature at the moment a tap would land (after floor(lag/16.67) or one more frames), and 'pop' needs both possible landings inside the window; waitOutcome looks one frame ahead and checks that a two-frame jump would still land in the window, a new popPending field blocks a second tap before the first one shows, and askWhen is true only at the tap moment so the approach keeps decisions about one frame apart (tickMs 16). The rules stay the same as v3.
instructions:
Pop the Lock. A bar spins around the centre of a ring and a dot sits on the ring. Tap while the bar is on the dot to pop it: the bar then turns the other way and the dot jumps elsewhere on the ring. Tapping while the bar is off the dot, or letting the bar pass the dot, ends the game. Pop as many dots as you can.
TIMING. The game never pauses. The bar turns stepDeg degrees (about 3) per animation frame (about 16.7 ms) in direction dir. A tap lands about 45 ms after the frame it is decided on, when two or three more frames have run, so by then the bar has turned about leadDeg further (about 8 degrees; 0 when the game waits for every decision). Every bar position below is therefore where the bar will be WHEN A TAP DECIDED NOW LANDS, not where it is drawn. While you are not consulted, decisions come about one frame apart; once you are consulted, the next decision comes only about one landing delay later.
FIELDS. barAngleDeg: the bar angle when a tap decided now lands. gapDeg: degrees that landing position is still short of the dot centre (negative = past the centre). gapNextDeg: the same for a tap decided one frame later. ticksToDot: frames until the landing position reaches the dot centre. barMoving: the bar moved since the last decision. barReversed: the bar just changed direction, which means a dot was just popped. dotMoving: the dot just jumped to a new place. dotPopped: the dot shown is the one just popped; the new dot has not appeared yet. popPending: the last tap moment was less than one landing delay ago and no pop has shown yet, so a tap decided then may still be on its way (a second tap would end the game). popTolDeg (5): the sure-pop window around the dot centre. edgeTolDeg (about 8): where the bar only touches the dot's edge.
THE 180-DEGREE LINE (the leftmost point of the ring): the game compares raw angles, so it never counts a hit across this line. seamSplit: the bar may land on the other side of the line from the dot; a tap then ends the game. barOnSeam: the bar may land exactly on the line, where the game may count it on either side, so a tap is a gamble. dotOnSeam: the dot sits exactly on the line and counts as the lower (negative-angle) side, so a tap is a gamble too.
A pop position is a bar position within popTolDeg of the dot centre, on the dot's side of the 180-degree line and not on it. A tap lands after two or three frames, so it is a sure pop only when both possible landing positions are pop positions.
tapOutcome = what a tap decided now does when it lands: 'pop' = sure pop (every possible landing is a pop position, the dot is not on the line, and the picture is settled); 'edge' = it may pop or may end the game (a landing only touches the dot's edge, or falls on the line); 'miss' = it ends the game; 'uncertain' = do not tap: the bar did not move or just reversed, the dot just jumped or was just popped, or popPending is true; 'none' = the game is over.
waitOutcome = what deciding again one frame later leads to: 'safe' = that later tap would still land short of the pop window (or there is no live dot yet); 'closer' = a tap one frame later would still be a sure pop and land nearer the dot centre (and, if a tap now is already a sure pop, it would stay a sure pop even if two frames pass), or the bar is crossing the 180-degree line and a tap two frames later is a sure pop; 'farther' = a tap one frame later would be a sure pop but would not land nearer the centre, or could stop being a sure pop if two frames pass; 'gameOver' = a tap one frame later may no longer be a sure pop (its landing passes the dot or reaches the 180-degree line), so now is the last chance.
RULES, in order: 1) gameOver is true -> wait. 2) tapOutcome is 'pop' and waitOutcome is 'farther' or 'gameOver' -> tap. 3) tapOutcome is 'edge' and waitOutcome is 'gameOver' -> tap (last chance: waiting loses the dot). 4) Otherwise -> wait. Never tap when tapOutcome is 'miss', 'uncertain' or 'none'. pops counts the dots popped so far; unknown lists unrecognised objects, which are not threats.

actions.description: Click the game once. If the bar is on the dot when the click lands, this pops it (the bar reverses and the dot jumps). If not, the game ends.
Do nothing for this decision and let the bar keep turning.

tests.why: One frame after a pop, the bar had reversed but the popped dot was still drawn at -176.1. v1 said 'pop', tapped again and lost. That dot must now be marked as popped and not tappable.
Same double-tap failure: the bar reversed from -12 to -15 while the popped dot stayed at -8.9.

tests.expect: !(state.barAngleDeg === 177 && state.dotAngleDeg === -177.1) || state.gameOver || (state.seamSplit === true && state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' && state.tapOutcome !== 'edge' && state.waitOutcome === 'closer')
tests.why: A tap with the bar at 177 and the dot at -177.1, on opposite sides of the +/-180 line, ended the game. The bar must wait until it crosses to the dot's side, which is also nearer the dot centre.
Keeps a known good pop: the bar 1.1 degrees from a settled dot and about to pass it must still be 'pop' at its best moment.
Keeps a known good pop: the bar 3.1 degrees before a settled dot, on the same side of the 180 line, must be recognised as poppable.

v2 tapped here and lost. The bar sat exactly on the 180-degree line (the old extractor showed -180) with the dot at -179, and the game counted the bar on the +180 side. A bar on the line must never be a sure pop. The next frame (-177) is a sure pop on the dot's side, so waiting must not be flagged as the last chance.
One frame earlier the bar is at 177, across the 180-degree line from the dot at -179. A tap there misses, and waiting leads through the line to a sure pop at -177.

tests.expect: state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' || (state.barOnSeam === false && state.seamSplit === false && state.dotOnSeam === false && Math.abs(state.gapDeg) <= state.popTolDeg)
tests.why: Invariant: a sure pop never has the bar or the dot on the 180-degree line or across it, and is always inside the sure-pop window.

tests.expect: state.tapOutcome !== 'pop' || (state.barOnSeam === false && state.seamSplit === false && state.dotOnSeam === false && Math.abs(state.gapDeg) <= state.popTolDeg)
tests.why: Same invariant on the first seam failure (bar 177, dot -177.1), which was recorded at the older, coarser tick.

A tap lands two or three frames later (leadDeg about 8), so this frame lands 1-4 deg before the centre and must be the tap moment.
